newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-NAVRATILOVA CONFIDENT OF FED CUP WIN OVER JAPAN.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-NAVRATILOVA CONFIDENT OF FED CUP WIN OVER JAPAN.

text.p: Fed Cup captain Martina Navratilova was feeling good about the chances of the United States winning its way back into the World Group after her squad's first on-site practice for the weekend tie against Japan.
"Everybody's healthy and ready to go," Navratilova said in a teleconference Tuesday after the Americans practiced at the Longwood Cricket Club.
"We know we're the overwhelming favourites," added Navratilova, who took over as U.S. captain this year only to watch the defending Fed Cup champions fall to the Netherlands in the opening round.
That surprise defeat in March put the United States in the unlikely position of having to win a playoff in order to compete for the Cup in 1998.
But Navratilova, who compiled a perfect 28-0 Fed Cup record as a player for Czechoslovakia and the United States, exuded confidence that competing at home would help her team carry the day.
"I'm definitely a lot more confident here than I was in Holland," Navratilova admitted. "If we had played that match here, I feel we would have beaten the Dutch."

Navratilova's team for the Saturday and Sunday best-of-five match tie is led by Olympic champion Lindsay Davenport, who helped the United States beat Spain in the 1996 final, and Cup veteran Mary Joe Fernandez.
Kimberly Po and Lisa Raymond complete the squad.

"I expect Mary Joe and Lindsay will be playing our singles matches, but I'm still playing around with different combinations for the doubles," Navratilova said. "We don't have to announce our doubles team until Friday and that will be after our last practice."
The draw for the tie will be held Friday at noon (1600 gmt) in downtown Boston.

"It's easy to get pumped for these matches because we're playing for our country and we have to win to get into the World Group One competition next year," said 13th-ranked Fernandez, who carries an 11-8 Fed Cup singles record into the tie, including wins that kept the 1996 U.S. title run alive.
With the retirement of Kimiko Date, the Japanese hopes rest with 34th-ranked Ai Sugiyama and 47th-ranked Naoko Sawamatsu, who Davenport called "two very difficult players."
"Their strength is foot speed, they take all the balls very early," said Davenport, who boasts a 12-2 Fed Cup singles record.
"If they have a weakness, it would be in their serves," added world number seven Davenport, who at 6-foot-3 (1.90 m) is nearly a foot (30 cm) taller than her singles opponents.
Said Navratilova: "On the hardcourt, the higher the bounce the better for us, because we're taller than they are."
